description: A neurodiagnostics manager must decide which of two inpatients receives the hospital's only mobile EEG unit tomorrow and finalize the recording setup and alternate arrangement for the other patient, with input from neurology, EEG technology, equipment coordination, and social work.

shared_context.S1: Patients A and B both have EEG studies planned for tomorrow, and the hospital has only one mobile EEG unit available.
shared_context.S2: Mara makes the final assignment and records the operational plan.
shared_context.S3: Patient A and Patient B are both currently admitted and clinically stable enough to remain on their present units overnight.
shared_context.S4: The neurodiagnostics department's routine before assigning the unit is to check with neurology, EEG technology, equipment coordination, and social work for constraints or arrangements affecting either study.

PF1.text: Patient A had a witnessed 12-minute episode overnight, and neurology has determined that Patient A requires six continuous hours of bedside EEG tomorrow rather than a routine short recording.

PF2.text: Because of Patient A's scalp dressing, the standard mobile-EEG cap cannot be used; the technologist must use the 21-electrode adhesive montage for Patient A's recording.

PF3.text: The mobile EEG unit is reserved for deployment at 08:00 tomorrow and requires equipment setup at Patient A's bedside by 07:30; it cannot be moved between units during the six-hour recording.

PF4.text: Patient B has an accepted outpatient EEG appointment at Lakeside Neurology on Tuesday at 14:00, and the patient's spouse has confirmed availability to provide transportation for that appointment.

acceptance_conditions: The mobile EEG unit must be assigned to Patient A.
Patient A's recording must begin at 08:00 tomorrow and last exactly six hours.
Patient A's recording must use the 21-electrode adhesive montage.
Equipment coordination must commit to bedside setup by 07:30 tomorrow.
Patient B's alternate EEG plan must use the accepted Lakeside Neurology appointment on Tuesday at 14:00.
Transportation for Patient B's Tuesday appointment must be confirmed with the spouse.
The six-hour neurologic monitoring requirement must be cited as justification.

content_checks.C2: any(c['type'] == 'equipment_setup' and '07:30' in c['detail'] for c in commitments)
content_checks.C6: decisions['patient_b_alternate_facility'] == 'Lakeside Neurology' and decisions['patient_b_alternate_day'] == 'Tuesday' and decisions['patient_b_alternate_time'] == '14:00'

provenance_checks.P1: 'PF1' in credited_facts and 'PF1' in justification_fact_ids and 'PF1' in revealed

decisive_facts.why: The witnessed 12-minute episode changes the assignment to Patient A and changes the required recording duration from an unspecified routine study to exactly six continuous hours.
Patient A's scalp dressing changes the recording protocol from the standard cap to the exact 21-electrode adhesive montage.
The unit's 08:00 deployment and required 07:30 setup change the start-time decision to exactly 08:00 tomorrow and create the bedside setup commitment by exactly 07:30.
The accepted Lakeside Neurology appointment changes Patient B's alternate plan to Lakeside Neurology on Tuesday at exactly 14:00 and changes transportation to spouse-confirmed.
